basis: Skin fragility and dental abnormalities define disease; oral blisters 80-99%. Chronic wound-related anemia occurs in 30-79%.
Periodontal destruction and connective-tissue abnormalities define disease; skin fragility 24/32 and atrophic scars 21/36 support skin involvement.
Congenital abnormal communication within the cardiovascular circulation.
Cerebellar degeneration defines disease; nystagmus is neurologic. Hearing impairment occurs in only 5-29%.
Intellectual disability, eyelid/eye defects and hearing loss define disease; dental hypoplasia 80-99%. Renal abnormalities and septal defects omitted by four-axis cap.
Heterotaxy includes congenital cardiac malformations; asplenia reported in 2/3 and hydronephrosis in 2/2. Small denominators limit certainty; situs alone is not organ damage.
Cortical body-localization disorder causing loss of recognition and orientation of body parts.
Red-cell membrane disorder causing hemolytic anemia and splenic enlargement; hemolytic jaundice does not establish hepatic injury.
Ovarian endocrine failure with hypergonadotropic hypogonadism and delayed puberty; gonadal hormone dysfunction has an endocrine axis.
GPI biosynthesis defect with encephalopathy; renal cysts/reflux and alacrima/ptosis each reported in 1/1. Skeletal abnormalities omitted by cap; frequency evidence is limited.
Peripheral nerve injury specifically caused by vitamin deficiency; both neuropathy and nutritional metabolic deficiency define the concept.
Congenital radius and ulna deformity with distal ulnar dislocation and restricted wrist movement.
Autoinflammatory syndrome establishes immune involvement; cold-triggered transient manifestations do not establish lasting organ damage.
Axonal peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy; distal weakness and amyotrophy reflect denervation rather than primary muscle disease.
Polyp occupies the sphenoidal sinus, which belongs to the upper respiratory tract.
Immune-mediated minimal-change podocyte disease causing nephrotic syndrome; steroid sensitivity supports this mechanism.
Ear defects, cleft palate and developmental disability define syndrome; thenar atrophy occurs in 30-79%. Renal fusion/ectopia alone does not establish functional injury.
Neoplasm originates in the endometrium, a reproductive tissue outside the organ axes.
Acute thyroid inflammation affects an endocrine gland; infectious and immune-mediated thyroiditis account for the principal forms.
Retinal cone dysfunction causes absent color discrimination, reduced acuity and photophobia.
Malignant neoplasm originating in the cerebral parietal lobe.
Treponemal infection umbrella; persistent skin, neurologic or cardiovascular injury is not established in most patients across the group.
Corneal endothelial dystrophy defines disease. Inguinal hernia occurs in 11/14 but does not itself establish direct injury to a locomotor or gastrointestinal organ.
Defined immune dysfunction and growth-hormone insensitivity support immune and endocrine axes; lymphoma susceptibility is a risk, not existing involvement.
Progressive skeletal myopathy with contractures; hypertrophic cardiomyopathy occurs in 4/7 (~57%). Respiratory insufficiency in 2/7 reflects muscle weakness.
